message: Documented penicillin allergy: cross-reactivity with cephalosporins is low (about 1-2%) but higher when the R1 side chain is similar (e.g. cefalexin, cefadroxil, cefaclor with amoxicillin/ampicillin).
recommendation: Prefer a cephalosporin with a dissimilar side chain (e.g. ceftriaxone, cefazolin) or a non-beta-lactam if the reaction was severe or IgE-mediated; confirm the allergy history before prescribing.
source: Pending clinical review (general allergy-practice parameter literature)

message: Documented penicillin allergy: cross-reactivity with carbapenems is rare (under 1%).
recommendation: Carbapenems can usually be given with monitoring; avoid if the reaction was a severe cutaneous adverse reaction.
source: Pending clinical review (general allergy-practice parameter literature)

message: Documented cephalosporin allergy: cross-reactivity with penicillins is possible when the side chains are similar.
recommendation: Confirm which cephalosporin and the reaction type before prescribing a penicillin.
source: Pending clinical review (general allergy-practice parameter literature)
